stories.headline: Army chief Dhiraj Seth: Land victory only tangible factor in war
stories.title: Army chief Dhiraj Seth: Land victory only tangible factor in war
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth on Sunday called a land victory the only "tangible factor" of success in a war, despite increasing technological innovations in the defence sector.

In his address at the NDTV Defence Summit 2016, General Seth said: "We see salvo after salvo in today's social media covering warfare across the globe, where information narratives and warfare are being fired to fog the real battle picture, creating uncertainty and confusion...
However, I strongly feel, through all this clutter, one reality that does not change: land will always be the one and only tangible and useful factor of success."
"Victory was, is, and will always be measured in territorial terms and that territory will be occupied, secured, and defended only by the force," he asserted.
"Every capability must address one question: how does it help that soldier who puts his boots or tracks on the ground?
That is why I would place him at the heart of the capability development that you're looking at..."

Recalling a photograph taken on December 16, 1971 that depicted Pakistan surrendering at the end of the Bangladesh Liberation War, the army chief said: "The reason I allude to this today is that photo gave us a very defining moment, because that was the precise moment when the war came to an end.
But there is no demarcating moment; there is no termination point which indicates an end to the hostilities."
He noted that conflict timelines are becoming "increasingly indefinite", with intermittent spikes of intense fighting.
"Technology is certainly shortening the battles, but it is not necessarily shortening the war.
These millennium wars can best be described as wars with pause.
Pause, in fact, is becoming a part of military strategy, with the pause representing not the domination of conflict but merely a change in its intensity and manifestation," General Seth added.

stories.headline: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.title: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy to reject the election petition preferred by former DMK Minister K.R. Periakaruppan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) rejected an election petition filed against the victory of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy from Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district by a razor-thin margin of just one vote in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Asepolls.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the TVK MLA to reject the election petition filed by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) candidate and former Minister K.R. Periakaruppan, who contended that he lost the polls primarily because of the existence of two Legislative Assembly constituencies with the same name ‘Tirupattur’ in Tamil Nadu.
Mr. Sethupathy was declared elected on securing 83,375 votes as against 83,374 votes garnered by Mr. Periakaruppan.

However, the DMK candidate claimed a postal vote belonging to the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district had been inadvertently sent to the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district and that the wrongly transferred vote was not sent back to the right constituency.

Listing out the reasons for seeking a rejection of the election petition, senior counsel V. Raghavachari, assisted by advocates Dixita Gohil and Pranjal Agarwal, argued the election petitioner had presented a “highly implausible” scenario of a postal vote belonging to one constituency having been sent to another constituency just because of their identical names.

He contended the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, make the identity of the intended constituency extremely difficult to lose by pressing into service multiple independent identifiers, which could enable the authorities to determine the constituency to which a postal ballot belongs.

The counsel pointed out the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district was identified as constituency number 50, whereas the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district was identified as constituency number 185.
He asserted that the constituency number, and not the name, was the key identifier.

He said every voter who intends to exercise his/her franchise through the postal ballot must make an application, using Form 12, to the Returning Officer concerned and therefore, the constituency gets determined emphatically even before the issuance of a postal ballot to an elector.

Further, the postal ballots have the full address of the Returning Officer of the relevant constituency pre-printed, without the need for the voters to fill it up by hand, and the postal covers too clearly mention the constituency name, number, district, and the full address of the Returning Officer.

“This means the postal ballot is not an anonymous page, which can ordinarily be treated as belonging to a constituency which happens to receive it by accident, coincidence, or otherwise,” Mr. Raghavachari said and added that it was the election officials who transport the postal covers.
The senior counsel also argued the election petitioner had not produced any material but for an affidavit filed by Tirupattur district DMK candidate.

stories.headline: Election Commission row: Mumbai Police deny CJP permission for October 2 protest at Shivaji Park
stories.title: Election Commission row: Mumbai Police deny CJP permission for October 2 protest at Shivaji Park
stories.summary: They cite court-imposed curbs on non-sporting activities at the ground, lack of BMC permission and concerns over noise and traffic congestion
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Mumbai Police have denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold a protest against the Election Commission at Shivaji Park on October 2, citing court-imposed restrictions on non-sporting activities at the ground, lack of BMC permission and concerns over noise and traffic congestion.
The Shivaji Park police conveyed the decision in a September 27 letter addressed to CJP national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde.
The party had sought permission to hold the protest at Shivaji Park in Dadar from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. on October 2.
The police primarily cited restrictions imposed by the Bombay High Court on the use of Shivaji Park for activities other than sports.
The notice referred to orders passed in a Public Interest Litigation petition of 2009, including a January 4, 2013 order concerning the use of the ground for non-sporting activities.
The High Court has previously restricted the use of Shivaji Park for non-sporting purposes, subject to specified exceptions and permissions.

The police also said the organisers had not submitted a permission letter for the use of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation-owned ground, as required under a Maharashtra government's Urban Development Department decision dated January 20, 2016.
The third ground cited was the possible impact of the proposed gathering on residents, traffic and hospitals in the vicinity.
“Since the said area is a peaceful and residential area, the possibility of noise pollution cannot be ruled out,” the police communication said.
It added that the protest could lead to “huge traffic” in and around Shivaji Park and said congestion could affect the movement of patients as several hospitals are located in the area.
Citing the High Court orders as well as the State government's 2016 decision, the police said permission for the October 2 protest at Shivaji Park and its surrounding area was being denied.
However, the police have not barred the CJP from holding a protest elsewhere in Mumbai.

stories.headline: Believe Bengal Speaker aware of deadline on TMC rebels disqualification: SC
stories.title: Believe Bengal Speaker aware of deadline on TMC rebels disqualification: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday said it has every reason to believe that the West Bengal Assembly speaker is "fully cognisant" of the apex court's order fixing a three-month time frame to decide the disqualification petition against 10 rebel TMC MLAs. The observations came from a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of a plea filed by Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction MLA Sohandeb Chattopadhyay. In his petition, Chattopadhyay sought direction to the speaker to expeditiously decide the disqualification petition filed against the rebel MLAs. "We have every reason to believe that the speaker is fully cognisant of the decision of this court and he will make an endeavour to take an appropriate decision within the time-frame fixed," the bench said while disposing of the plea. The top court noted that in this case, the three-month period would expire on October 10. Chattopadhyay had earlier approached Speaker Rathin Bose

stories.headline: Blueleaf Energy Acquires 40 MW Operating Wind Asset in Karnataka
stories.title: Blueleaf Energy Acquires 40 MW Operating Wind Asset in Karnataka
stories.summary: Pan-Asian renewable energy platform Blueleaf Energy has acquired a 40 MW operating wind power asset in Karnataka’s Belagavi district. The operational wind farm has eight years of clean energy generation experience and complements Blueleaf Energy’s existing 1.5 GW greenfield portfolio across India. It includes projects under construction and in operation. The company secured its legal, finance, and tax structuring advice from Talwar Thakore & Associates (TT&A) and EY. “This acquisition marks an important milestone as our first operating asset purchase in India. Building upon our established success in greenfield development, we are now pursuing targeted M&A to accelerate our growth and scale our presence while maintaining a strong focus on delivering long-term value for India’s clean energy transition,” said Pratyush Thakur, Country Head, India, Blueleaf Energy. Blueleaf Energy’s Previous Projects in India Previously, Blueleaf Energy, commissioned its 300 MWp Pachora Hybrid Power Project in Madhya Pradesh. The project is jointly owned by Blueleaf Energy and Jakson Green through its parent company, Jakson Limited. The utility-scale wind and solar project has an estimated value of approximately ₹1,900 crore. The merchant project is expected to generate nearly 600 million units (MU) of clean electricity annually, which will be sold on the Indian power market. Blueleaf Energy has also established a presence in Rajasthan through its partnership with Jakson Green, with 280 MWp and 560 MWp ground-mounted solar plants in Bikaner forming part of the 1 GWp Rajasthan Solar Portfolio. The partners recently achieved financial close for the portfolio with Axis Bank, marking the completion of funding for the entirety of the portfolio.

stories.headline: Supreme Court urges West Bengal Assembly Speaker to decide disqualification petitions within October 8
stories.title: Supreme Court urges West Bengal Assembly Speaker to decide disqualification petitions within October 8
stories.summary: The court had suggested three months to be a reasonable time unless exceptional circumstances exist
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) urged the Speaker of the West Bengal State Legislative Assembly to conclude the disqualification proceedings initiated by former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool Congress faction against rival Ritabrata Banerjee faction under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution for alleged defection by October 8, 2026.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocates Kapil Sibal, Vivek Tankha and advocate Preetika Dwivedi, appearing for the Mamata Banerjee camp, said the apex court had held in the Keisham Meghachandra Singh versus Speaker, Manipur Legislative Assembly judgment that the Assembly Speaker, acting as a Tribunal under the anti-defection law of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, must decide disqualification petitions within a “reasonable time”.
The court had suggested three months to be a reasonable time unless exceptional circumstances exist.
“The three months expire on October 8.
This has become a pattern.
The Speaker does not deal with the disqualification petitions.
The rebel MLAs go to the Election Commission (EC) and get an interim order,” Mr. Sibal submitted.

The senior counsel was referring to an interim order of the EC on September 17 freezing the TMC party symbol and name in order to “place both the rival groups on an even keel and to protect their rights and interests”.

But the Chief Justice expressed reluctance in intervening in the case, saying it would instead pass an order expressing “hope that the Speaker will follow the law laid down in the Meghachandra judgement.”
Mr. Sibal said the court must examine this “pattern” or it would create “political havoc”.
“There are statutes where the judiciary is required to complete proceedings within a time frame.
We are gloriously in breach of that, so how can we tell the Speaker?” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, posed to Mr. Sibal in a lighter vein.

stories.headline: | Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR Show Systematic Failure Of Police & Administration : Supreme Court Takes Suo Motu Cognizance
stories.title: BREAKING | Rape Cases In Delhi-NCR Show Systematic Failure Of Police & Administration : Supreme Court Takes Suo Motu Cognizance
stories.summary: Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil; accountability must be fixed upon authorities, the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil; accountability must be fixed upon authorities, the Court said.

The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognizance of recent cases of rape in Delhi-NCR, including a gangrape in a park and the alleged sexual assault of a minor inside a moving sleeper bus in Delhi.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran observed that they were distressed by the news reports regarding recurring sexual offences in the National Capital Region, and stressed the need to fix accountability.
In the order, the bench referred to the gangrape and murder of a teenage girl in Swarup Nagar in Delhi, where the police recovered the victim's decomposed body in a field.

Referring to the sexual assault of a minor in a moving sleeping bus, which the police failed to intercept during its travel of 47 kilometres from Greater Noida to Delhi, the Court said that “one cannot help but draw painful parallels to the Nirbhaya incident of 2012.”
These incidents raise the question whether the systematic law enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress since the Nirbhaya case, the Court observed.

"These incidents considered alongside other recent reports of sexual offences across Delhi-NCR starkly underline a systematic failure on the part of the law enforcement and the public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety," the bench observed.
The right to live with dignity free from the fear of violence is an intrinsic facet of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution.

Public spaces, including roads, parks, buses, metro stations, subways, footbridges, cannot be permitted to become "zones of high risk" due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lack of patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies.

The bench stated that the statements made by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concerns and solidarity are not enough, and said accountability had to be fixed for failures that contributed to such incidents.
“Expressions of solidarity devoid of accountability fall short of answering the larger institutional question.
Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil.

stories.headline: 1947 promises, not 2019, should Be reference point for J&K: Sajad Lone
stories.title: 1947 promises, not 2019, should Be reference point for J&K: Sajad Lone
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 28 : Peoples Conference president and MLA Sajad Lone on Monday said that the commitments made in 1947 should remain the reference point for any discussion on Jammu and Kashmir’s political status and its relationship with India. Speaking in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly, as per news agency—Kashmir News Observer(KNO), Lone said he had “full respect” for the Prime Minister and the Supreme Court, but asserted that Jammu and Kashmir’s presence within India was rooted in the commitments made to its people in 1947. “I have full respect for the Prime Minister of India and the Supreme Court of India. But if we are here today, it is not because of any promise made by the Prime Minister or the Supreme Court. We are here because of the promises made to the people of J&K in 1947,” Lone said. He said the original framework envisaged a structure in which the people of Jammu and Kashmir would have a meaningful say in their governance and would enjoy autonomy and powers to take their own decisions. Questioning the constitutional and legal basis of the Centre’s decision to reorganise Jammu and Kashmir as a Union Territory, Lone asked, “Tell me, the Union government that relegated us — is this within the limits of law or not?” Referring to the Supreme Court judgment, Lone said the Court had not answered all questions surrounding whether a state could be converted into a Union Territory in such circumstances. He said the Assembly should not shift its historical reference point while discussing Jammu and Kashmir. “The reference point in this Assembly should be 1947, not 2019. We cannot change the reference point. We cannot change the contours of history,” Lone said. Lone also said political phases and governments would change with time, but the historical commitments made to the people of Jammu and Kashmir should continue to be considered. “This is a phase. How many came and how many went. They will also go one day. You will also go one day. We are also in a phase,” he said. “We should not change the reference point. The reference point has to be 1947,” Lone added.—(KNO)

stories.headline: RBI expected to raise repo rate by 50 bps in FY27
stories.title: RBI expected to raise repo rate by 50 bps in FY27
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in title weight 42
article_sentences: New Delhi: India's GDP growth in the second quarter of FY2026-27 came in significantly above the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 7 per cent forecast, prompting expectations of a gradual rate-hiking cycle, according to a HSBC Global Investment Research report.
The report expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points twice in FY27, taking it to 5.75 per cent, as economic growth remains strong and inflationary pressures persist.
"Q2 FY26 GDP growth has come in much higher than the RBI's 7 per cent forecast.
Furthermore, the RBI expects inflation to average more than 5 per cent over the next three quarters.
This combination, we believe, opens the door for gentle rate hikes," the report said.
It also expects the RBI to absorb Rs 5-6 trillion of excess liquidity created by FCNR(B) deposits through durable measures such as open market operation (OMO) sales.
According to the report, inflation is expected to remain close to the RBI's 4 per cent target in the first half of FY27 before rising in the second half.
Headline inflation is projected to average above 5 per cent over the next nine months.
"Brent oil prices have rebounded after briefly falling in June.
El Nino conditions are likely to strengthen in the December quarter, potentially pushing food inflation higher," the report said.
It added that higher input costs could be passed on to consumers by companies, which may push core inflation towards 5 per cent by the end of FY27.
India's GDP growth for the quarter ended June stood at 7.8 per cent.
